newsitem.title: USA: Indiana city most affordable U.S. housing market.
newsitem.headline: Indiana city most affordable U.S. housing market.

text.p: The small Indiana city of Kokomo, Ind., offered the most affordable housing in the country during the first quarter this year, the National Association of Home Builders said on Thursday.
According to the builders' specially constructed Housing Opportunity Index, Kokomo topped a list of 190 metropolitan areas for affordability with a reading of 89.5 percent.
That meant a Kokomo family earning the median income for the region of $46,000 could have qualified to buy 89.5 percent of the homes sold there in the first three months this year.
The median price of a Kokomo home was $85,000. The median marks the mid-point, with half the homes sold going for less than $85,000 and half for more than that price.
Waht was the least affordable market?
San Francisco, by a long shot, at 23 percent.
A San Francisco family earning the median income in the area of $64,400 could have afforded just 23 percent of the homes that changed hands in the first quarter this year.
Little wonder, since the median price of a San Francisco home was $288,000 -- the highest in the country.

The affordability index measures the proportion of homes sold in a specific market that a family earning a median income could qualify to buy. It takes into account differences in property tax rates and in property insurance rates in each community.
Nationally, housing affordability improved slightly during the first three months of 1997 from the final quarter of last year, rising to 66.5 percent from 64.1 percent.

The median sale price of a home nationally was $120,000 in the first quarter, the same as in the fourth quarter last year. But the national median income was up to $43,500 from $41,600, so potential buyers could afford more.
Kent Colton, chief executive officer of the builders' association, said "stable and relatively low" mortgage interest rates were bolstering the housing market.
An average long-term loan rate of 7.75 percent was used in calculating the first-quarter affordability index, up only fractionally from 7.73 percent in the final quarter last year.

The top five affordable housing areas, with their relative affordability and median sales prices, were: Kokomo, Ind. (89.5 percent, $85,000); Baton Rouge, La. (88.9 percent, $85,000); Beaumont, Port Arthur, Tex. (86.1 percent, $72,000); Elmira, N.Y. (86.1 percent, $60,000), and Wilmington-Newark, Del. (86 percent, $119,000).

The five least affordable were as follows: San Francisco (23 percent, $288,000); Portland-Vancouver, Ore. (30.8 percent, $147,000); Laredo, Tex. (34 percent, $90,000); Santa Cruz-Watsonville, Calif. (35.4 percent, $217,000), and Santa Rosa, Calif. (35.6 percent, $190,000).
